modules.title: 只有一个实例时，请求和重启风险集中在哪里
单实例部署要先看清什么

items.title: 唯一副本决定了可用性窗口
items.text: 服务只有一个运行实例时，发布、崩溃或维护期间没有其他副本可以接管服务请求。重启期间出现短暂不可用是预期风险，不应把部署任务成功误认为用户始终可访问。

items.title: 把必须保留的状态移出进程内存
items.text: 实例停止后，进程内存里的未完成任务可能消失；数据库或其他持久存储中的记录则可以在服务恢复后重新读取。验收要分别检查服务是否恢复、持久化数据是否还在，以及哪些内存任务允许丢失；这样能改善恢复判断，但不能让单实例自动拥有故障接管能力。

items.title: 内部会议室预约也可以单实例运行
items.text: 访问量很小的内部预约服务可以只运行一个实例，部署更简单；但发布时所有预约入口会一起短暂不可用，因此应选择可接受的维护时段并明确这项风险。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 单实例部署描述的是运行中的副本数，不是代码里的单例模式；一个单实例服务仍可以使用数据库保存数据，也不代表它不能扩展。它的核心边界是同一时刻只有一个实例承接服务请求，因此重启和实例故障没有同服务副本立即接管。

lessonPractice.title: 单实例服务正在重启，用户暂时打不开页面。哪种判断和验收最准确？

options.label: 承认重启期间可能短暂不可用，确认服务恢复后持久化数据仍能读到
options.feedback: 对。单实例的可用性风险集中在唯一副本，但持久化数据是否保留要单独验证。

options.label: 把代码里的单例对象删掉，就能让部署变成多实例并避免中断
options.feedback: 单例模式是代码结构，不能改变运行环境中服务副本的数量或重启行为。

options.label: 只要服务重新显示在线，重启前放在内存里的任务就一定还在
options.feedback: 进程内存通常会随实例停止而消失；恢复在线不能证明内存任务被保存。

en.title: A single-instance service is restarting and users temporarily cannot open the page. Which judgment and verification are accurate?

options.label: Accept a brief restart outage and confirm durable data is readable after recovery
options.feedback: Correct. Availability risk is concentrated in the only replica, while data durability must be verified separately.

options.label: Delete the Singleton object in code to make deployment multi-instance and avoid the interruption
options.feedback: The Singleton pattern is a code structure; it cannot change runtime replica count or restart behavior.

options.label: Once the service is online again, assume every task kept in memory before restart still exists
options.feedback: Process memory normally disappears when the instance stops; recovery does not prove in-memory work was saved.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请把这个后台服务按单实例部署，并明确写出副本数为 1 时的重启不可用窗口。检查任务状态是否写入持久存储，不要把必须恢复的任务只放在进程内存。改完后重启一次，确认服务恢复、已有数据仍可读取，并告诉我单实例带来的可用性风险。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Deploy this background service as a single instance and state the restart unavailability window when the replica count is 1. Check that task state is written to durable storage instead of keeping recoverable work only in process memory. Restart it once, confirm the service recovers and existing data is readable, and report the availability risk of the single instance.

learning.assumes: You know a service runs in an environment where it can be restarted or replaced.
learning.outcome: You can identify which availability and in-memory-state risks concentrate in one instance and state how to verify them.

modules.title: Where request and restart risk concentrates with one instance
What to see clearly in single-instance deployment

items.title: The only replica defines the availability window
items.text: When one running instance handles the service, a release, crash, or maintenance event leaves no other replica of the same service to take over requests. Brief unavailability during restart is an expected risk; a successful deployment job does not mean users remain continuously connected.

items.title: Move required state out of process memory
items.text: Unfinished work in process memory may disappear when the instance stops, while records in durable storage can be read again after recovery. Verify service recovery, durable data, and which in-memory tasks may be lost separately. This improves recovery evidence but does not give one instance automatic failover.

items.title: An internal room-booking service can run as one instance
items.text: A low-traffic internal room-booking service can run as one instance for a simpler deployment. However, every booking entry point becomes briefly unavailable during a release, so choose an acceptable maintenance window and state this risk clearly.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: Single-instance deployment describes the number of running replicas, not a Singleton code pattern. A single-instance service can still use a database and can later scale. Its key boundary is that only one service instance is available to receive requests, so restart and instance failure have no same-service replica ready to take over immediately.
